description: Almost everyone gets creator marketing backwards. They pay for the biggest following they can afford and spend it all at the top. But at the awareness stage, a creator saves you about 5% of the customer journey. At the interest stage, when someone's already considering a product like yours, it's 39%. That's the whole game. So don't blow it on one giant name. Spread it across 3 to 5 smaller creators who actually live in your category, where people are already decided. #InfluencerMarketing #CreatorEconomy #TikTokShop #Ecommerce #MarketingStrategy
transcript: There was a popular beauty brand that did tens of millions on TikTok Shop, and the vast majority of it came from affiliate creators, not their own account, not paid ads. So creators aren't a nice to have? They're the channel. The question is how do you deploy them? And almost everyone gets it backwards. They pay a big creator for awareness, the biggest following they can afford. But at the awareness stage, a creator saves you about 5% of the customer journey time. At the interest stage, when someone's already considering a product like yours, 39%. That's the whole game. Your creator budget moves the needle in the middle, not at the top. So don't blow it on one giant name. Spread it across three or five smaller creators who actually live in your category, deployed where people are already deciding and watch what a real recommendation does now. In the long run, you need to scale that out to hundreds if not thousands of creators. That's what the companies generating millions if not tens of millions of dollars a year from TikTok are doing.
